entry_state: Chapter3 separates literal accuracy, proposed meaning, purpose admission and accounting eligibility; the156/163 navigation conflict illustrates distinct correct query answers. Coverage has three populations, precision needs a rounding assumption, and investor/system views require different exact-byte evidence. The bank baseline and treaty-order examples distinguish corrected knowledge from economic timing. Section3.14.2 now explains candidate-set invalidation and ancestry; its final committed-journal distinction continues on73.

findings.judgment: Retrying the exact original financing event returns its original receipt; changing its request under the same business identity is a conflict. Revised treaty chronology alone supplies no authority for a correcting journal. TREATMENT_UNSUPPORTED retains a conditional calculation without posting.

Accounting conservation does not define admissible transactions; dynamic models supply behavioural examples rather than universal defaults. Labelled unknowns preserve dependence; provenance composition is not a posterior. Identification and model averaging require additional assumptions, and the mixed accounting setting inherits no general theorem from a continuous inverse problem.

A shared typed representation permits a library/DSL comparison. Catala conflict semantics, LegalMath interpretation and ACTUS contract transitions each solve a narrower problem than accounting-history reconstruction. TableFormer separates supplied PDF words from predicted cell structure; its95.4/90.1/93.6 TEDS figures cannot establish complete-filing semantic accuracy. FinQA-style answers, RAG provenance and a completed sampler remain distinct from company histories.

sections/sector-revision.tex:section:1.entry_belief: Eligibility and supersession now have defined information cutoffs.
sections/sector-revision.tex:section:1.open_question: What happens when a later fact changes a sector measurement?
sections/sector-revision.tex:section:1.parent_contribution: Connects information revision to credit baselines, treaty recognition and transactional persistence.
sections/sector-revision.tex:section:1.belief_update: An irrevocable commitment remains the bank risk baseline; treaty entry order changes recognized balances. A new record can change the candidate set even when the selected assertion or displayed answer stays the same.
sections/sector-revision.tex:section:1.exit_question: When is an accounting correction justified rather than merely a revised reconstruction?

sections/sector-revision.tex:section:1.swap_verdict: It needs exact-byte timing and source-selection rules before showing their sector consequences.

sections/sector-revision.tex:section:1.exit_verdict: No correction entry is created without applicable treatment, period and account support.
sections/sector-revision.tex:section:1.promise_verdict: Authored January dates and supplied numerical paths are specification fixtures, not actual historical-availability or actuarial findings.
sections/sector-revision.tex:section:1.distinct_contribution_verdict: A changed conclusion, a preserved earlier explanation and a committed journal can all legitimately coexist.

sections/sector-revision.tex:subsection:.open_question: What must be invalidated, and what must an exact retry preserve?

sections/sector-revision.tex:subsection:.exit_question: Which literature can support these semantics without being mistaken for their full proof?

sections/sector-revision.tex:subsection:.swap_verdict: The before/after treaty case supplies the changed input before this dependency rule is stated.
sections/sector-revision.tex:subsection:.entry_verdict: The unchanged selected identifier is the concrete cache-reuse trap.
sections/sector-revision.tex:subsection:.exit_verdict: Versioning records a proposed correction but cannot supply its accounting authority.

chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.entry_belief: A coherent representation still needs justification for its accounting and economic structures.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.open_question: Which accounting models transfer, and which assumptions must be chosen afresh?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.parent_contribution: Distinguishes algebraic conservation, transaction admissibility, behavioural dynamics and sector constraints.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.belief_update: Nehmer/Robinson support state conservation; Doshi supports explicit time/corrections; Shahnazarian/Pierson support separating accounting accumulation from behavior. Bank papers motivate state and management interfaces without calibrating this application.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.exit_question: How can incomplete disclosures and shared unknowns be represented?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.removal_verdict: The architecture would lack a grounded distinction between balanced accounts and admissible economic evolution.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.swap_verdict: Accounting structure appropriately precedes database and inference ideas.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.entry_verdict: The algebraic state-space contribution is tied immediately to the posting validator.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.exit_verdict: REA and stock-flow-consistent traditions remain named source gaps with no borrowed technical results.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.promise_verdict: No universal payment-delay, equity, portfolio or tax-data default is inferred from the examples.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:1.distinct_contribution_verdict: Accounting identities constrain evolution but do not identify behavior or permissible events.

chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.entry_belief: Published reports can be consistent with more than one underlying record.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.open_question: What do incomplete databases, provenance and temporal storage contribute?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.parent_contribution: Grounds shared unknowns, query certainty, compositional provenance and historical views.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.belief_update: Certain answers hold across a nonempty declared family, with existential information beyond listed certain rows. Positive provenance semirings do not cover all nonlinear/negative operations; public availability extends beyond database transaction time.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.exit_question: What can inference learn when the disclosures do not identify a unique history?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.removal_verdict: Independent missing cells or citation lists would lose the dependence and derivation structure the product requires.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.swap_verdict: This establishes the information problem before proposing inversion or probabilities.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.entry_verdict: Multiple records producing the same reports makes database incompleteness substantive.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.exit_verdict: An insertion timestamp cannot establish what an investor could know.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.promise_verdict: Libkin supplies inspected technical support; the inaccessible Imielinski/Lipski source remains a backward lead, not a silently inspected authority.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:2.distinct_contribution_verdict: Representation preserves dependence and provenance without assigning probability mass.

chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.entry_belief: A family of possible histories and their provenance is available in principle.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.open_question: When can inversion or probability narrow that family?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.parent_contribution: Separates identification, regularisation, Bayesian measures and scenario interventions.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.belief_update: A flat likelihood cannot learn the unidentified conditional prior. Model averaging needs priors and marginal likelihoods and cannot weight duplicated encodings. Stress interventions differ from conditioning on historical high-rate observations.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.exit_question: Which language structures can express these conditional rules and contracts?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.removal_verdict: A solver witness or convenient prior could otherwise be mistaken for identification from reports.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.swap_verdict: Its inference distinctions depend on the incomplete-information representation just established.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.entry_verdict: The observation equation introduces inversion through the same reports-to-hidden-history problem.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.exit_verdict: Pearl clarifies why reproducing accounts cannot identify a causal effect.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.promise_verdict: Neither infinite-dimensional well-posedness nor SVAR robust-inference guarantees transfers automatically to mixed discontinuous accounting programs.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:3.distinct_contribution_verdict: Additional assumptions can define an inference task while leaving evidence-driven identification incomplete.

chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.entry_belief: The system must express rules, alternatives, contracts and optional inference.

chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.belief_update: One shared IR permits library and textual authoring. Rule conflict differs from evidence-supported alternatives; bounded candidate search is not a complete family. Contract payoffs remain separate from recognition and measurement.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.exit_question: Which extraction evidence supports importing source assertions into that representation?
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.removal_verdict: Syntax or an existing rule language could otherwise be selected as if it solved inverse-history semantics.
chapters/03-literature.tex:section:4.swap_verdict: Representation and inference requirements give the language comparison its evaluation tasks.

Chapter4 has examined accounting dynamics, incomplete databases, provenance, identification, rule languages, extraction and inference. These supply bounded design ideas with explicit transfer limits; blocked foundational papers remain omissions. Sections4.1–4.6 are read;4.7 and the chapter conclusion remain next.
